decisions: Is DDPM sampling a good replacement for current GAN generation stack?

requirements.description: How bad is the sampling speed really? Are we talking milliseconds or full seconds per image compared to our current GANs?
Is the training actually stable unlike GANs which are known for instability like mode collapse?
What are some major hyperparameters that may be required to tune for decent results or are hyperparameters adaptable for multiple datasets?
Do the images look sharp in the examples, or is there a trade-off for the stability we get?

decisions: Implementation Strategy: Defining the hardware budget and architectural specifics.

requirements.description: What is the GPU memory footprint for training a standard 256x256 model? Do we need a cluster or just a single node?
Does the architecture require expensive self-attention at high resolutions, or can we optimize that out?
How parallelizable is the training since diffusion is inherently sequential in sampling?
Are there specific initialization tricks mentioned that prevent the model from outputting pure noise at the start?
Does the paper rely on TPU-specific operations, or is it standard PyTorch/TensorFlow code we can port easily?

decisions: Architecture Selection: Choosing the Best 'Connector' and LLM Backbone.

requirements.description: Which visual connector (e.g., Q-Former vs. Projection) is the lightweight winner for speed?
Which models are flagged as 'hallucination prone'? We need to know which ones make up things that aren't there.
What’s the VRAM requirement? What specific components drive that requirement the most in Audio, Video or Image modalities?
Are features like 'OCR-free reading' actually working well in these models, or is that just marketing hype?
Does the review identify a clear dominating model/backbone for multiple modalities (e.g. Qwen vs. Llama vs. Vicuna)?
Is the licensing for the top models actually permissible for commercial use, or is it research-only?
Which models are open weights with LoRA adaptable methods or are they all closed weights?

decisions: Data & Training Pipeline: Determining how much effort allows us to ship.

requirements.description: Does the review say massive data is non-negotiable? Can we get away with a small, high-quality datasets
Do we absolutely have to pre-train from scratch, or does the survey point to fine-tuning pre-trained models as a viable path for getting great results or is there a tradeoff?
Are automated metrics like POPE or MME reliable enough to be our main unit test, or do we need humans?
How hard is it to add new modalities to existing models(like Audio) later if we pick a specific architecture now?
Does instruction tuning tends to make the model 'forget' its original text-only capabilities?
Are there simple recipes for 'alignment' to stop the model from generating toxic descriptions of images?

decisions: Deployment Feasibility: Can we consolidate our audio stack into Qwen2-Audio?

requirements.description: Will this model fit on our standard inference GPUs (e.g., 24GB VRAM), or is it too big?
Is the latency low enough for a conversation, or is there a noticeable lag before it starts responding?
Is there a hard limit on audio length (like 30 seconds) that would break our use case for long files?
How does it handle noisy audio or background chatter? Does it fail or just transcribe the noise?
Does it refuse to process certain audio types (safety refusals) that might be false positives for us?
Can we swap out the audio encoder part later, or is it tightly coupled to the Qwen text model?

decisions: Integration & Capabilities: Verifying it meets our specific product needs.

requirements.description: Does it support sound event detection (e.g., 'glass breaking') or is it strictly for speech-to-text?
How well does it handle multiple speakers? Can it distinguish 'Speaker A' from 'Speaker B'?
Is fine-tuning supported (e.g. LoRA) if we need to teach it specific medical or technical vocabulary?
Does the 'voice chat' mode support interruption, or do we have to wait for it to finish speaking?
What is the cost-per-minute compared to just using a cheap ASR API like Whisper?

decisions: Evaluating Flow Matching vs. Autoregressive Models.

requirements.description: Is this actually faster than VALL-E in a real production setting, or just theoretically faster?
Do we need expensive phoneme-alignment data to train this, or can we just throw raw audio+text at it?
Does the voice start to sound weird or 'drift' if we generate a really long paragraph?
Are there any watermark detectors included, or do we have to build our own safety checks?
Is the 'flow matching' more stable than existing methods, or does training often diverge and fail?
Can we run this on standard consumer GPUs or does it require massive H100 clusters?
Can it cleanly fix a bad word in a recording without making a 'click' or pop sound at the edit point?
How short can the voice sample be for cloning? Can it work with a 3-second clip?
Does it support cross-lingual stuff out of the box (like making an English speaker speak French)?
Does it also work as a denoiser? Can we feed it noisy audio and get clean speech out?
How well does it capture the emotion of the prompt? Does it sound robotic or expressive?
Are the pre-trained weights available vis the survey, or is this paper purely academic with no code?

decisions: How feasible is it to use Tree-Ring Watermarking for Rectified Flow Models (FLUX).

requirements.description: What are some benchmarks for evaluating the watermark detection and how relevant is it for our use case?
Are we screwed if we lose the original text prompt? Can we use a VLM to guess it and still detect the watermark reliably?
How fragile is the detection? Does slight cropping or resizing of the image break it completely?
Is the 'noise inversion' step significantly harder or slower on Flow models compared to the standard DDIM inversion we use for SD 2.1?
Do we need to store the specific 'key' and 'mask' for every single image we generate, or is there a universal key?
Does embedding this watermark in the Fourier space visible degrade the image quality?

decisions: Benchmarking: Comparing FLUX.1-dev robustness against Stable Diffusion 2.1.

requirements.description: Why does FLUX perform worse under attack compared to SD 2.1? Is the latent space just more sensitive to noise?
Does using a VLM to generate the inversion prompt actually work, or is the reconstruction error (NMSE) still too high to be useful?
What is the false positive rate? Can we statistically separate a watermarked FLUX image from a random noise image with high confidence?
Do we need to tweak the watermark radius or channel parameters specifically for FLUX, or can we use the same settings as SD?
If we don't provide any prompt at all during detection ('No Prompt'), is the system effectively blind?
Is the 'Latent Noise Reconstruction' metric stable enough to be our primary automated check for copyright compliance?
